evidence.scope: The two autonomous transitions in this design, lazy rent accrual and deterministic eviction, at their boundaries and inside a swap.

gates.note: Rent accrual is asserted to be exactly rent times elapsed blocks, idempotent within one block, and to charge nothing with no manager; eviction is asserted to land on the exhausting block, to cap the charge at the remaining deposit, to reset the seat and never to revert a swap.

evidence.scope: Residual AMM amount, charge bounds, full-consumption rejection and partial-fill rejection on the two beforeSwap quadrants, with fuzz coverage of the magnitude range.

gates.note: The two beforeSwap-charged quadrants are asserted on the specified amount, the charge is bounded at one wei below the executed amount so a zero AMM leg cannot occur, and a partial fill on either quadrant reverts rather than charging unexecuted volume.

evidence.scope: Four-quadrant swap execution through core, which rejects a wrong selector or return-data length, plus a raw-router bypass attempt that is charged identically. It does not include a dedicated malformed-selector negative test.

evidence.scope: Authorization and clamping of the only input to the LP fee, plus the seat-rotation rules that bound who can move it. There is no pool-state observation to manipulate, so no same-block observation attack is modelled.
evidence.command: forge test --match-contract AuctionTest && forge test --match-contract FuzzTest

gates.note: The fee input is a stored parameter of a paid role rather than a pool observation, so the manipulation surface is the role itself: only the current manager may set it, an evicted manager cannot, the value is clamped, a handover resets it to the default, and the seat can only move through the auction.
